result.rationale: The diff adds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, followed by `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Since a template literal always yields a non-empty string, the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` (and its newly added locale string) is unreachable, and when `err.data?.code` is undefined the toast shows a literal 'undefined: ' prefix with a raw error code, confirming the described mechanism. This is a real, verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

judged_text: The error-toast fallback is dead code: `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` `` is a template literal that is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never render the fallback, and when err.data.code is absent the toast shows a literal 'undefined: …' prefix. Users always see raw machine-shaped error strings instead of the intended friendly message; the unable_to_add_guests fallback and its new locale string can never display.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` which always produces a non-empty string (e.g. `"undefined: ..."` when `err.data?.code` is missing). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` can never hit the fallback, making `unable_to_add_guests` effectively unreachable and potentially showing a literal `undefined:` prefix to users.
